exposure: maternal biological factors (hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, intrauterine growth restriction, chronic hypertension)
outcome: neonatal morbidity (admission to the neonatal unit, days of hospitalization, jaundice)
cohort: The study included early-term newborns and full-term newborns.
finding: Early-term newborns had a 1.9-fold higher probability of morbidity at birth compared to full-term newborns, with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, intrauterine growth restriction, and chronic hypertension identified as maternal biological factors associated with early term birth.
gest_age: Early-term newborns (37 and 38 weeks) and full-term newborns.
